subject: Subprocessor delegation: vendor-chain consent & signature sequencing
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marie Coleman <marie.coleman@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessor list + flow-down path for Order Form redlines

Marie —

Thanks for the call today. Quick follow-up as we pull the Order Form and MSA redlines together for procurement and legal: could you send the current subprocessor roster (including geographic locations and whether subprocessor access is limited to encrypted logs only) and confirm:

- Whether CloudBridge expects unrestricted cascade consent (i.e., broad right to delegate to new subs without separate notice), or whether you require prior written consent for additions outside the named roster.
- If you propose a DPA exhibit, please share the latest version.
- Any standard flow-down language you expect on the Order Form (e.g., paragraph that binds subcontractors to our DPA terms).

I've attached our internal Order Form with the redlines Jordan flagged — primary ask is to align on acceptance path and signature sequencing so procurement and DocuSign flow don't block launch. We're trying to avoid a long legal loop.

Attachments: OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf

Thanks — appreciate a short summary and the spreadsheet if you have one.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Redwood Inference | Production-first inference for developer teams

From: Marie Coleman <marie.coleman@cloudbridge.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cloudbridge.com>, contracts@cloudbridge.com
Date: 2027-03-09T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list + flow-down path for Order Form redlines

Lukas —

Thanks for the note. Attaching the current subprocessor roster (CloudBridge_Subproc_List_v3.xlsx). Short answers up front:

- Cascade consent: Our standard is to name an initial roster, and allow the addition of new subprocessors with prior notice; for sensitive data categories we require written consent. We can accept a clause that permits additions with 14-day notice unless the customer objects in writing.
- DPA: see attached DPA exhibit (we keep it lightweight) — we will accept your DPA redline in many cases but ask for a mutual indemnity carve-out for covered security incidents caused by subcontractors.
- Flow-down on Order Form: we typically request a sentence that requires subcontractors to comply with the DPA and provides audit rights to the controller.

We reviewed your tracked OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf; the main negotiation points for us are:
1) Audit scope (limitation to SOC2 evidence vs. broader onsite audits)
2) Data deletion timing for cached logs
3) The subcontracting consent clause (we'd like the 14-day notice + objection model)

If you want to limit execution risk, we can sign the current order form conditioned on a separate annex that enumerates current subprocessors and the 14-day addition notice.

Attaching: CloudBridge_Subproc_List_v3.xlsx

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with legal and procurement next week to finalize.

Best,
Marie Coleman
Senior Counsel — Contracts | CloudBridge Inc.
marie.coleman@cloudbridge.com

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Subprocessor list + flow-down path for Order Form redlines

Kimberly —

Forwarding CloudBridge's response and the subprocessor roster. High level: they propose a 14-day notice + objection model for additions and want an annex listing current subprocessors; they flagged a mutual indemnity carve-out tied to subcontractor-caused incidents.

Can you advise:
- Is 14-day notice + objection acceptable for our risk profile?
- Are we OK moving audit rights to reliance on SOC2 evidence or do we require onsite audit language for specific categories?
- If we accept the annex approach, do we need any additional contract language to preserve our remediation rights?

I've attached their spreadsheet and our redlines again. Jordan — FYI on sequencing: if legal is comfortable, we want to proceed with DocuSign envelope and post-sign annexing of the roster to avoid blocking go-live.

Thanks,
Lukas

Attachment: CloudBridge_Subproc_List_v3.xlsx, OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Subprocessor list + flow-down path for Order Form redlines

Team —

Reviewed CloudBridge's materials and Lukas/Jordan's proposed sequencing. Notes below and attached a redline PDF with comments (Redline_MSAs_Lukas_KP_comments.pdf):

1) 14-day notice + objection: workable, but we should limit what constitutes a valid objection to material changes in processing (e.g., new subprocessors in a different jurisdiction or with access to plain-text user content). That keeps them from gaming the model with low-risk infra vendors.

2) Audit rights: accept SOC 2 evidence as the primary mechanism; retain the right to request targeted onsite audits for escrows or if evidence indicates gaps. Proposed language in redline: "Customer may rely on audit reports and may request an on-site audit only upon demonstration of reasonable cause."

3) Annex approach: acceptable. We should add a one-time "post-signing acknowledgment" process where CloudBridge must deliver an executed annex listing current subprocessors within 10 business days of signature. That way DocuSign can proceed while the annex is formalized.

4) Indemnity carve-out: push back on an open-ended mutual carve-out. We can agree to limited liability for subcontractor-caused incidents where CloudBridge fails to exercise reasonable care. Wording in the redline reflects that scope.

Next steps I recommend:
- Lukas/Jordan initiate DocuSign on the Order Form with the conditional annex checkbox and a link to the DocuSign envelope in the cover email.
- Laura to confirm procurement PO/term conditions (Laura, pls advise if any PO gating is required before signature).
- If CloudBridge accepts, we will provide a short annex template for their roster.

Attaching: Redline_MSAs_Lukas_KP_comments.pdf

Kimberly Park
Associate Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marie Coleman <marie.coleman@cloudbridge.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-11T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list + flow-down path for Order Form redlines

Marie — Lukas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the roster. We're aligned on the conditional annex approach and Kim's redlines look good. From sales/procurement perspective:

- We'll send the DocuSign envelope today with the Order Form and a checkbox confirming CloudBridge will deliver the executed annex within 10 business days.
- Procurement (Laura) — please confirm if a PO is required before DocuSign or if we can proceed with supply under the signed Order Form and follow with PO.
- Marie, once the envelope is out, please have contracts@cloudbridge.com review Kim's redline and confirm acceptance of the 14-day notice + objection model with the objections limited as Kim suggested.

If all good, target signature by EOD Friday and annex execution by next week.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
